text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov dismissed the head of the National Intelligence Service Brigo Asparuhov at the request of the interim government and replaced him with Dimo Gyaurov, a former deputy of the main anti-leftist coalition Union of Democratic Forces. @

-- Jeffrey Sachs, director of the Harvard Institute of Development, is expected to hold talks in Sofia on Friday with President Petar Stoyanov and with interim cabinet' members on the country's economic stabilisation measures.
-- Bulgaria is expected to agree on a funding programme for implementation of a currency board system with the International Monetary Fund next week, deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said.
-- Railway passenger fares will rise 2.5 times from March 20, Transport ministry decided. @
-- A poll among Bulgarian Army soldiers showed that 76 of the army staff supported Bulgaria's bid for a full NATO membership, deputy defence minister Roumen Kanchev said.

-- Bulgaria's interim cabinet decided to abolish visa requirements for nationals of the European Union and the European Free Trade Association visiting for up to 30 days, foreign minister Stoyan Stalev said. @

-- Bulgaria has overcome recent fuel shortages and fuel will be readily available at petrol stations throughout the country within two weeks, the head of Bulgaria's largest oil refinery Neftochim Nikola Karagyozov said.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank foreign exchange reserves rose by $30.5 million in February to $445.5 million, the bank said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
